I’m 54 now, and I don’t like making big changes unless I’ve seen with my own eyes they pay. On my 42 mu, I’ll still keep the wheat-maize land as the backbone, because grain keeps the household steady. I’ll put 20 mu into wheat, and after harvest that same 20 mu goes straight into summer maize. The rest I’ll keep in cash crops: 14 mu cotton and 8 mu cucumber. Cucumber brings money fastest, but it eats labor and inputs, so I won’t spread it too wide. Cotton is slower money, but I know how to manage it. Wheat and maize I won’t cut too hard on fertilizer, because if the stand turns weak, that loss hurts more than saving a little cash. I have well water, so I’ll use it, but not too many times because pumping costs real money. Mostly I’ll do what has worked on my land: enough fertilizer to keep the crop from looking hungry, split once or twice when needed, and watch the field myself instead of chasing fancy methods.
